maya: Heads up — saw a reproducible latency spike on TP training jobs (8-way) during step boundaries. 20-80ms spikes, looks like all-reduce backpressure.

maya: Attached a tiny profile dump. trace shows a long series of tiny NCCL allreduce ops instead of a few large ones. KC cache flush + batching heuristics seem involved.

maya: snippet from perf (summary):
```
msg_size(bytes)  count  p50_allreduce_ms
64               4200   0.9
512              1200   2.1
8192             80     7.8
65536            5      18.4
```

maya: interestingly, when msg_size < ~1KB we see NCCL picking a tree-like algorithm for some ranks and ring for others (split policy?), leads to serialization stalls.

tony: can you paste the NCCL env + kernel selection logs? also which runtime build?

maya: runtime: v1.23.4-runtime, compiled kernels: optimized-int8 and float16 paths. NCCL version 2.13.3. env: `NCCL_ALGO=auto NCCL_PROTO=collnet` (weird, collnet enabled by default on these boxes)

lee: collnet can cause unexpected fallbacks on heterogeneous link topologies. also small messages + collnet/tree interplay can blow up latency. try forcing ring for a run: `export NCCL_ALGO=ring NCCL_PROTO=Simple` and repro.

sam: iirc we had a KV cache flush path that emits many tiny reduce ops when kv shards are evicted during prefix cache misses. might be a batching heuristic bug — we flush per-key rather than coalescing across keys.

maya: yes — the trace shows a burst of 3-5 small reductions each step tied to `kvcache_shard_flush()`. When we increase the internal coalesce window to 8ms the number of ops drops by ~80% and p50 drops ~12ms.

maya: quick repro command i used: `./bench_tp --model=redwood-tp --micro-batch=1 --steps=200 --trace=allreduce` then prof -> `python parse_trace.py trace.json --agg-by=msg_size`

tony: nice. sounds like two levers: 1) runtime batching/coalesce 2) force consistent NCCL algo across ranks (avoid mixed ring/tree). Both cheap to try. Kernel selection might also mis-handle pinned vs staged buffers.

lee: pinned buffers note: if send buffer isn't pinned we get extra memcpy->staging which amplifies latency for tiny msgs. check `USE_PINNED_SEND=true` path. also make sure our kernel chooser picks the kernel that writes into pinned region.

sam: i can add a small change to delay kv-flush until either size threshold or coalesce window elapsed. will run A/B to see throughput vs latency tradeoff.

maya: plan: (1) @sam add coalesce window patch + perf test, (2) @lee run forced ring vs auto on the same job, (3) @tony add a small diag to log chosen NCCL algo per-rank at startup so we detect mixed modes.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline started: run-tp-latency-checks (#249). CI will run 3 seeds across 8 GPUs. ETA ~45m.

maya: thanks — if CI repros i'll open a perf regression ticket and label `root-cause: batching-heuristic`/`mitigation: pinned-buffers`.

tony: also add a synthetic microbench that simulates kvcache eviction patterns so we don't regress this again.

maya: if anyone has quick hypotheses on kernel selection heuristics causing fragmentation lmk. otherwise i'll wait for CI results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
